newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- NOV 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- NOV 28.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--One of the biggest general strikes in recent years gets under way in Greece today as the General Confederation of Workers of Greece (GSEE) and civil servants are joined by taxi-drivers. The repurcussions on public transport, industry and services are expected to be enormous.

--Just one day after the official presentation of the government's economic policy, internal and social pressure has caused a turn around: the planned across the board abolition of tax breaks has been adapted to excluding the abolition of tax breaks for MPs, airline pilots and journalists for this year.

--No bridges were built at last night's meeting of the conservative opposition New Democracy's Political Council. Former prime minister Constantine Mitsotakis, lately very vocal in his criticism of ND leader Miltiades Evert, was told he was no longer welcome at Political Council meetings. Mitsotakis replied he didn't care to come.

--An MP belonging to Turkey's ruling party confessed to Turkish television viewers that members of the shadowy terrorist organisation 'The Grey Wolves' were involved in setting forest fires on Greek islands.
--A new bill aims to reorganise public transport, with mergers, debt write-offs and private firms taking responsibility for ticket inspection.
--The water company will face charges for not clearing drains in the Piraeus area, following an inquiry into flooding last month.
--Greece goes on strike:The general strike which began at midnight hits every sector, from industry and public transport to hospitals and schools. Farmers have warned they will block national roads.

--Tansu Ciller, Turkey's foreign minister, is implicated in claims made last week that Turkish terrorists set fires on Greek islands two years ago, while she was prime minister. The claims were made by a member of Ciller's party.
--Unionists warn that more industrial action is on the cards for December.
--Evert throws Mitsotakis out of the party's Political Council and fails to agree with his main contender for the leadership George Souflias on how to conduct the party congress.

--Some 110 MPs rushed to get their luxury cars before their tax exemptions were cut, reports say. The Mercedes dealer, the reports add, ran out of stock, forcing some 50 MPs to resort to Saab and other luxury cars.
--Interior Minister Alekos Papadopoulos warns he is ready to sack civil servants found to be in breach of the rules of conduct. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
